radiology_report:
Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Department of Radiology
Date: 28 Feb 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA to 2.7 ng/mL with prior negative biopsy; assessment for PI-RADS scoring.

FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 56.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a homogeneous peripheral zone without discrete mass lesions. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows no focal restricted diffusion, and dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal no early focal enhancement. A small, well-circumscribed 8 mm area of mild T2 hypointensity is noted in the left anterior peripheral zone, demonstrating isointense diffusion and no wash-in on DCE, consistent with benign prostatic hyperplasia or focal prostatitis. The central gland shows typical age-related hyperplastic changes. Neurovascular bundles are intact. No seminal vesicle invasion or pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified.

IMPRESSION: Benign-appearing peripheral zone finding without suspicious focal lesion. PI-RADS v2.1 score: 2. PSA density: 0.05 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage: cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.48990974.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient attended for follow-up of a mildly elevated prostate-specific antigen level of 2.1 ng/mL detected on routine screening. A transperineal systematic biopsy was arranged and performed without complications, with results subsequently communicated to the patient indicating benign prostatic tissue. Given the persistent but slow PSA rise and the patient's severe lower urinary tract symptoms, a referral to urology was initiated for comprehensive re-evaluation and discussion of long-term management options.

pathology_report:
Specimen: Transperineal systematic biopsy (05 Mar 2024)
Microscopic examination of the submitted prostatic tissue cores reveals benign glandular architecture with no evidence of malignancy. The glands are lined by a single layer of epithelial cells without nuclear atypia or architectural distortion. The final histological diagnosis is benign prostatic tissue, corresponding to a Gleason score of 0+0 and ISUP Grade Group 0.

Trajectory summary: Histological evaluation across the available biopsy timepoint remains stable with no malignant features identified.
